clue.text: Important people who are the opposite of a shady character

indicators.note: being the opposite here means the word for the shady character is turned round end to end

parts.note: a spiv is a flashy small-time crook or black-market dealer

explanation.surface: A description of worthy dignitaries as the antithesis of crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the opposite of' turns SPIV, a British word for a flashy wheeler-dealer, round to give VIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: VIPs are very important persons, people of high standing or celebrity.

clue.text: Vehicle in which top person holds king up over endless river

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first part above the second
the important person's letters hold the turned king inside them

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the king's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Old King Cole is the nursery-rhyme king

indicators.note: endless says the river's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the Eden is a river in Cumbria, England

explanation.surface: A carriage in which a dignitary lifts a monarch above a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns COLE into ELOC; 'holds' puts it in VIP; 'endless' cuts EDEN to EDE, placed below by 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A velocipede is an early bicycle or tricycle, a pedal-driven vehicle.

clue.text: Controversial measure preceding extraordinary claim

indicators.note: preceding places the measure before the rest

parts.note: a pole is an old unit of length

indicators.note: extraordinary indicates the letters of the next word are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: A divisive yardstick ahead of a remarkable assertion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges CLAIM into MICAL. A pole (also rod or perch) is an old British measure of 5.5 yards.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical means argumentative and disputatious, given to attacking opinions.

clue.text: I reduce the honourable in me as a means of making myself heard

definitions.text: a means of making myself heard

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the word me, which opens to take them

parts.note: taken as written
to crop is to cut short or reduce
Hon is the standard abbreviation for the title Honourable

explanation.surface: Someone speaking about cutting a dignitary down to size in order to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a speaker cutting someone down; 'in' is the container signal, and 'me' is fodder, not the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A microphone amplifies the voice so a speaker can be heard by a crowd.

clue.text: Way of entering to make the painter second

parts.note: Ingres was a French neoclassical painter

explanation.surface: A way into making an artist come second.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a 19th-century French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act or means of going in, an entrance.

clue.text: Responded to performance in the grass

indicators.note: the performance word is placed inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Reaction to a show staged among the grasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Responded to performance' reads as one phrase, but 'to' is only a link; the definition is 'Responded' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Reacted means answered or behaved in reply to something.

clue.text: Precise article about a country holding a dance for an important dancer

parts.note: prim means precise and proper
a is the indefinite article
a ball is a formal dance
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A prim piece of writing about a nation hosting a ball, for a star dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run PRIM, A, BALL, ERIN, A; 'about' and 'holding' do not fit the order cleanly and read as surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima ballerina is the leading female dancer of a ballet company.

clue.text: 'Organ which has twitch after medical treatment

indicators.note: after places the twitch word following the treatment word

parts.note: op is short for a surgical operation
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A body part that develops a spasm following surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray opening quote mark is a printing artefact. 'Organ' is the eye, not a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an informal word for the eye, the organ of sight.

clue.text: In the afterthought this nobleman would give precious things to a woman

definitions.text: In the afterthought this nobleman would give precious things to a woman

parts.words: In the afterthought this nobleman would give precious things to a woman
parts.note: an afterthought is a postscript, PS; put the peer inside those two letters and you get gems on a string, a gift of jewellery for a lady

explanation.surface: A lord whose PS promises jewels to a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Put this peer inside PS (postscript, 'the afterthought') and you get PEARLS, 'precious things to a woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount.

clue.text: They stretch from pole to pole and are not members of a classless society

definitions.text: They stretch from pole to pole and are not members of a classless society

parts.words: They stretch from pole to pole and are not members of a classless society
parts.note: the word runs from S to N, south pole to north pole, and its members all belong to forms or classes

explanation.surface: A people spanning the globe who belong to a class.
explanation.walkthrough: The word begins with S and ends with N, the two poles; pupils are by definition in a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolchildren are pupils, all assigned to classes at school.

clue.text: I go in to ring back for something for the garden

indicators.note: the letter I enters the other piece, sitting inside it
back says the word for ring is read in reverse

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the telephone

explanation.surface: Someone saying they'll pop in to return a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CALL into LLAC; 'go in to' places I inside it after the first L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a flowering shrub commonly planted in gardens.

clue.text: This fighter is a happy one before the order is reversed

parts.note: glad means happy
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for the order is read backwards, as the clue states outright

parts.note: a rota is a list giving the order in which people take turns

explanation.surface: A cheerful combatant whose sequence gets flipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy one' reads as a single idea but gives two pieces; 'is reversed' turns the duty list round, and 'the order' means a rota, not a command.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a Roman arena combatant who fought for public entertainment.

clue.text: Examination which makes the ordinary seem attractive

parts.note: common means ordinary or everyday
to entrance is to charm or enchant, making something seem attractive

explanation.surface: A test that can make plain things look glamorous.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'entrance' as the verb meaning to enchant, not a way in. The Common Entrance is the British exam pupils take, usually at 13, to enter independent senior schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Entrance is a British admission test for fee-paying secondary schools.

clue.text: This reproduces documents so that the missing youth is found in the vehicle

indicators.note: the missing youth turns up inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a cycle is a bicycle, a vehicle
lost means missing
Y is an abbreviation for young or youth

explanation.surface: A lost child turns up in a car, which is how papers get copied.
explanation.walkthrough: Y for youth is a dictionary abbreviation; a cyclostyle was an office stencil copier, long obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclostyle was a stencil duplicator used for copying papers.

clue.text: Unusual policeman likes troublesome children

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters appear in an unexpected rearranged order

parts.note: PC stands for police constable

explanation.surface: An odd police officer who is fond of mischievous kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges PC plus LIKES.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is an informal British term for a mischievous child.

clue.text: System of government which puts a distinguished man into the record book

indicators.note: the letters for the honour go into the middle of the book word

parts.note: a diary is a book in which daily events are recorded
CH is Companion of Honour, a British award for distinguished service

explanation.surface: A regime that enters a notable person into the annals.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order of distinction, so it stands for a distinguished person.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarchy is rule shared by two authorities, a dual government.

clue.text: On occasion among those referred to as being arrogant

indicators.note: the occasion word goes among the letters of the other

parts.note: cited means referred to or quoted
once means on one occasion

explanation.surface: People sometimes mentioned as being haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those referred to' looks like people, but it is the participle 'cited'.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited means vain and self-important, full of pride.

clue.text: Oracular state in which I help reforms

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit within the two-letter abbreviation for the state

parts.note: DC, the District of Columbia, is treated here as a state

indicators.note: reforms suggests the letters are re-formed into a new order

explanation.surface: A nation in which a helper changes how things are done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' turns I HELP into ELPHI. Washington DC is not strictly a state, a liberty crosswords often take.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphic means ambiguous and prophetic, like the oracle at Delphi.

clue.text: Discipline to make the child start to hurry

indicators.note: start tells us to take just the opening letter of the child word

parts.note: to hasten is to hurry

explanation.surface: Telling off a youngster to get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes C from 'child', then HASTEN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to correct or restrain, to discipline.

clue.text: Officer has a company with a single beginner

parts.note: lone means single or solitary
L is a learner, the plate shown by a British learner driver

explanation.surface: An army officer who keeps one novice in his unit.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate, so L stands for a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army rank, just below brigadier.

clue.text: Tobacco gives one something academic before an examination

indicators.note: before places the headwear ahead of the exam

parts.note: a cap, as in mortarboard, is academic headwear
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: Smoking material handed to a student before a viva.
explanation.walkthrough: A mortarboard cap is part of academic dress; an oral is a spoken exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Caporal is a strong dark French tobacco.

clue.text: The workers are the ones who scoff about the route to the seaside place

indicators.note: about tells us the scoffers' word wraps around the other two pieces

parts.note: railers are people who rail, jeer or scoff
a way is a route
a port is a coastal town

explanation.surface: Mockers ridiculing the road to a coastal resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ones who scoff' is a noun built from 'rail', meaning to complain or jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway porters were station employees who carried passengers' luggage.

clue.text: Mountains in Scotland esteemed for "their ruggedness

indicators.note: in shows the answer is tucked inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Peaks in Scotland admired for their rugged look.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'scotlANDESteemed'; Scotland is a false lead, these peaks are in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain range of South America.

clue.text: Opposite of something cold for ruler of hot place

indicators.note: opposite here means the cold word is turned to face the other way

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: The reverse of chill suits a sovereign in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposite of' turns RIME (frost) round.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or prince, often of a desert Arab state.

clue.text: Church leader who takes a revolutionary' back in his car

indicators.note: the reversed pair is carried inside the vehicle word

parts.note: motor is a British informal word for a car

indicators.note: back turns both little pieces around together

parts.note: red is a common label for a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A clergyman giving a radical a lift in his vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A RED into DERA. In Presbyterian churches the moderator presides over the assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: A moderator presides over a Presbyterian church court or general assembly.

clue.text: Smart denial about a race

indicators.note: the word for denial goes around the race letters

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a denial
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A stylish refusal to take part in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the famous Isle of Man motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and fashionably dressed, dapper.

clue.text: Depend on including a drunkard embracing a woman noisily

indicators.note: the depend word opens up to include the next part

parts.note: to rely is to depend on

indicators.note: the drunkard's word holds the woman's name within it

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
Nan is a woman's name, short for Ann

explanation.surface: Relying on a drunk who hugs a woman, all making a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' makes SONANT. Nan as a woman's name is a crossword staple, a pet form of Ann.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonantly means with a deep, ringing, echoing sound, so loudly.

clue.text: Border in which this particular weed generally flourishes

indicators.note: in which points to letters running inside the following words

explanation.surface: A garden edge where a certain weed thrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'weED GEnerally'; 'this particular' and 'flourishes' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the border or rim of something.
